text:
Carolina made it three wins in a row in Seattle by making the Kraken chase the puck all night. Sebastian Aho scored twice, including a power-play tip-in 66 seconds after Nikolaj Ehlers opened the scoring, and the game was effectively settled before the second period was half over. Aho was drafted 35th overall in 2015 out of Karpat Jr., and he now has a steady hand in a team that keeps stacking wins.

How the game was really played matches the score. Our expected goals figure, which measures the quality of chances rather than the goals themselves, favored CAR 3.23 to 2.01, and the Hurricanes took 84 shot attempts to SEA's 37. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave CAR 71 percent. The second period was the one stretch Seattle held its own, matching Carolina's chances almost exactly, and Ben Meyers had the best look of the night, a 26 percent chance that Brandon Bussi stopped. Bussi saved about one goal more than the shots he faced should have cost him, while Philipp Grubauer allowed about three-quarters of a goal more than expected on the other end. Juuso Välimäki added a snap shot for the third goal and put four shots on net.

Seattle got on the board late, when Frederick Gaudreau scored at 13:15 of the third, 94 seconds after Aho's second goal made it 4-0. The Hurricanes are now on a three-game winning streak, and the Kraken head into their next game having gone 0 for 2 on the power play with little to show for 13 shots on goal.
